userStories.title: Claude native interrupt seam and real-SDK gate
userStories.description: As an Archon engine, I want a per-turn interrupt signal wired to Claude's native Query.interrupt() and a proven session-id contract, so that one Claude turn can be stopped without invoking node Cancel while every non-interrupt call stays byte-for-byte on the existing prompt/abort path.
acceptanceCriteria: AgentRequestOptions gains optional `interruptSignal?: AbortSignal`; `abortSignal` remains the node Cancel signal (packages/providers/src/types.ts ~line 593).

ProviderCapabilities gains a REQUIRED `interrupt: 'native' | 'stream-abort' | false` axis; Claude and e2e-fake are 'native'; Codex, Grok, Copilot, DeepSeek, Devin, OMP, OpenCode, Pi, and Qoder CLI are `false`; every concrete provider registration and test fixture declares it without casts or optional escape hatches.

MessageChunk result type gains optional `terminalReason?: string`, passed through from the SDK result's `terminal_reason`; no inference from prose/tool text; existing is_interrupt → toolOutcome 'interrupted' mapping and session/usage fields preserved.
Calls WITHOUT interruptSignal keep the existing string-prompt path and all current abort/close/retry behavior unchanged (regression tests prove the SDK receives the same string prompt).

Calls WITH interruptSignal use the typed one-message AsyncIterable<SDKUserMessage> the pin expects, kept open for the query lifetime via a provider-owned deferred settled in every result/error/Cancel/finally path.

Turn interruptSignal abort calls native `query.interrupt()` exactly once (including repeated abort notification) and never aborts the SDK controller or closes the query; node abortSignal retains existing abort+close and never calls native interrupt; both listeners are removed in finally including early consumer return.

A pre-aborted interruptSignal is checked before every SDK retry attempt so a spent turn starts/restarts no query; an interrupted attempt is never retried; native interrupt promise rejection is surfaced through the provider stream (no unhandled rejection or silent hang).

scripts/generate-capability-matrix.ts renders a total Interrupt row with `native`/`stream-abort`/❌ cells (not a collapsed boolean) and packages/docs-web/src/content/docs/reference/provider-capabilities.md is regenerated; `bun run generate:capability-matrix` and `bun run check:capability-matrix` pass.

New diagnostic spike script packages/providers/src/claude/interrupt-resume-spike.ts (modeled on askhuman-resume-spike.ts) is added with a `spike:interrupt:claude` package.json script (not exported); the real-SDK gate exercises new-session interrupt, resumed-session interrupt, event ordering, terminal reason, control acknowledgement incl. still_queued, query completion with open iterator, and same-session continuation.

The sanitized report reports/claude-interrupt-resume-spike.md records command, SDK pin (0.3.209), event ordering, terminal reason, session-id equality, and outcome — no prompts, credentials, or model content. If the gate cannot retain a trustworthy session id, STOP and record the blocker instead of inventing a session id or downgrading to Cancel.

All phase-1 'Tests first' items are covered: string-prompt regression, streaming-input shape, exactly-once native interrupt, Cancel-vs-interrupt separation, terminalReason normalization shape, pre-aborted no-start, rejection surfacing, listener/iterator cleanup on all exit paths, no retry of interrupted attempts.
`cd packages/providers && bun test src/claude/provider.test.ts -t 'interrupt' && bun test src/registry.test.ts && bun test src/observability.test.ts && bun run type-check` all pass.
userStories.technicalNotes: Follow phase-01-claude-native-interrupt-seam.md and plan decisions D1–D3. Spike is diagnostic, not CI — unit tests use the mocked SDK only after the observed event sequence is known. Do not expose the capability axis through the server provider-catalog schema (no current caller). Capability is an implementation-mechanism declaration, not UI state.
userStories.notes: Implemented in iteration 1. Files: packages/providers/src/types.ts (interruptSignal, interrupt axis, terminalReason), claude/provider.ts (streaming-input path, native interrupt binding, pending-flush, no-retry, listener/gate cleanup), claude/interrupt-resume-spike.ts + spike:interrupt:claude, 11 capabilities.ts files, generate-capability-matrix.ts + regenerated doc, tests in claude/codex/e2e-fake/registry. Real-SDK gate: protocol interrupt-turn-resume, session-id equality proven; sanitized report at reports/claude-interrupt-resume-spike.md.

userStories.title: Registry tokenized turns, executor classification, and idle-await
userStories.description: As an Archon engine, I want race-safe live-turn tracking, five-case end classification, and explicit idle-await with atomic send_now release inside the existing steering handle, so that an interrupted Claude turn idles on the same session and a redirect resumes it without losing or duplicating any accepted receipt — across direct AI nodes, AI loops, and provider-calling loop-group bodies.
acceptanceCriteria: steering-registry.ts: `register(runId, nodeId, { interruptible })` reuses a live/parked handle only when interruptibility agrees, else fails fast; existing process singleton, live|parked|closed phase, receipt-order queue, accepted-id memory, and synchronous last gate preserved.

beginTurn(controller) returns a monotonically increasing token, starts `generating`, is valid only on a live interruptible handle, and fails fast until the prior token is settled; endTurnStream(token) clears only the matching controller (stale token = safe no-op); settleTurn(token, outcome) resolves only that token's pending interrupt once (stale/duplicate = safe no-op).

interrupt() synchronously aborts the currently stored turn controller, sets the operator-interrupt flag once, and returns one shared settlement promise; repeated calls share it; idle calls return idle immediately; calls after endTurnStream but before settleTurn wait for classification and never abort an old controller; settling clears the flag so a resumed turn cannot inherit stale interruption state.
Settlement values cover idle-after-interrupt, generating, node_finished, and internal not_steerable_here; close/park/discard/clear settle all pending interrupt and idle waiters exactly once.

Single synchronous accept(message, intent) mutation replaces separate enqueue/state/send-now ops: duplicate ids replay original receipt without re-enqueue/release; new message while generating → `queued`; while idle → `awaiting_send_now`; intent 'queue' while idle leaves waiter unresolved; intent 'send_now' while idle appends the non-blank message, drains whole queue in receipt order, moves handle to generating, resolves waiter — all in the same tick; send_now while generating/interrupting queues normally; receipts are immutable (awaiting_send_now never rewritten to queued).

enterIdle(token) projects idle-after-interrupt, resolves an in-flight interrupt as idle, returns one waiter carrying drained batch or terminal wake reason; first of Send now / handle discard / cancel-status poll wins; natural empty terminal → node_finished; park/unavailable → not_steerable_here; run discard wakes executor onto existing Cancel path; test clear leaves no unresolved promises; projected steeringSubState exists only for live interruptible handles and is exactly generating | idle-after-interrupt.

dag-executor.ts threads a FRESH interrupt controller through every runStreamPass invocation (each provider pass, including re-asks and guidance turns — never reused) only when the resolved provider capability is interruptible; registers it immediately before sendQuery, passes interruptSignal, captures terminalReason/result/session/operator-flag, calls endTurnStream in finally and settleTurn after classification; direct AI path (~line 3002 register), AI loop path (~line 5673), and loop-group namespaced body path all behave identically (loop-group proven by test, no third implementation).

Five-case end classification implemented in positional order: node/iteration Cancel checked first (unchanged); typed interrupt terminal reason recognized BEFORE the generic msg.isError failure guard (abort-marked + operator flag → interrupted even with isError/error subtype; unmarked error → genuine failure); interrupted end skips the entire structured-output validation/re-ask block before batch emission, credit exhaustion, empty-output failure, natural queue drain, loop completion checks, or node completion; Stop racing a natural unmarked result retains normal validation but the operator-interrupt flag joins canReask so no further provider pass starts; throw → interrupted only when matching turn operator-interrupted + signal aborted + narrow helper recognizes abort name/code/message (unrelated error racing Stop = genuine failure, tested).
Claude interrupt marker is exactly terminalReason === 'aborted_streaming' || 'aborted_tools' — no broad prefix, no result-presence inference, no prose classification.

Interrupted end preserves accounting: per-pass usage recorder runs, cost/tokens fold into node/loop totals exactly once; no batch-send of partial assistant text, no text-based credit/empty-output classifiers, no loop completion evaluation on the partial; abort-marked result overrides the wait-for-live-background-Agent-tasks rule (no announce, no follow-up wait, no generic incomplete-task warning); redirected turn retains accumulated usage/cost — budget enforcement not reset/bypassed.

Tool/status settlement: abort-marked interrupted result closes remaining runningTools entries as `interrupted` BEFORE the existing map clear; provider-emitted interrupted tool_result retained without duplication; interrupted throw settles still-open entries before leaving map scope; idle entry writes exactly ONE status row with state `interrupted` (awaited before enterIdle resolves the interrupt request so a committed transcript outcome precedes UI); existing agent-history fold applies the following interrupted row to the preceding tool card; no node_failed/dag_node_failed/completion/validation-miss events for interrupted turns.

Boundaries: natural result + pending queue → fresh session id required, drain, settle interrupt route as generating, next outer turn; natural result + empty queue → closeIfEmpty() seal, settle node_finished, normal completion; interrupted result/throw → verified resumable session id required, enter idle even with queued messages; Send-now wake joins drained messages with existing double-newline convention, fresh transcript attempt, next turn on the interrupted turn's session id; missing session id before drain or idle = fail-fast node error with queue intact and no fresh provider session.
AI-loop redirect runs inside the same iteration before until/until_field/until_bash/interactive-gate/max-iteration decisions and does not increment the iteration count.

Idle-await exits only via atomic send_now, same-process discardRun wake, or a scoped cancel-status timer using CANCEL_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS + shouldContinueStreamingForStatus stopped on every wake; NO 30-minute inactivity timer (Story 2.12).

All phase-2 registry tests (9 items) and the 15-scenario executor matrix pass, including abort-marked result after Stop → idle, abort-marked + isError → idle not failed, abort-like throw → idle no dag_node_failed, natural wins + queue → generating drain, natural wins + empty → finished, Cancel co-fire → Cancel wins, no re-ask after Stop, exactly-one-interrupted per tool + one status row, no background wait, usage retained once, two-old-plus-new Send now → one next turn double-newline receipt order same session, missing session id → explicit failure, idle discard/remote cancel → cleanup + terminal path, second interrupt after resume → fresh token no stale flag.

`cd packages/workflows && bun test src/steering-registry.test.ts && bun test src/dag-executor.test.ts -t 'interrupt' && bun test src/dag-executor.test.ts -t 'queued guidance' && bun run type-check && cd ../.. && bun --filter @archon/workflows test` all pass; existing Cancel, AskHuman park/resume, credit limits, and Story 2.1 natural-drain tests still green.
userStories.technicalNotes: Follow phase-02-engine-registry-turns-and-idle-await.md and plan decisions D4–D6. dag-executor.ts has duplicated direct/loop stream handling — share only small pure classification/types if it reduces divergence; no unrelated executor refactor. Highest data-integrity risk: clearing runningTools before marking interrupted — tests must assert persisted row order, not only returned state. Depends on US-001's interruptSignal + terminalReason + capability axis.
userStories.notes: Implemented in iteration 2. Files: packages/workflows/src/steering-registry.ts (interruptible register, beginTurn/endTurnStream/settleTurn/interrupt, accept intent, enterIdle, steeringSubState), packages/workflows/src/dag-executor.ts (fresh interruptSignal per pass, five-case classification in direct + AI-loop + loop-group paths, interrupted tool/status settlement, idle-await raceIdleWake, same-session send_now redirect), tests in steering-registry.test.ts (57 tests) and dag-executor.test.ts (19-scenario matrix). Validation: tsc, eslint, prettier, focused + full @archon/workflows suite all green.

userStories.title: Interrupt route, atomic Send now, and sub-state projection
userStories.description: As an operator, I want an interrupt endpoint that reports the engine's actual classified outcome and a GET-run projection that exposes the live steering sub-state, so that the dock can render Stop/Send-now truthfully without any durable state being invented.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/workflows/runs/{runId}/nodes/{nodeId}/interrupt registered via registerOpenApiRoute(createRoute({...})) with no request body; awaits executor settlement and returns only the actual outcome: 200 `{success:true, sub_state:'idle-after-interrupt'}`, 200 `{success:true, sub_state:'generating'}`, or 409 `node_finished` — never a timing-based guess.

Interrupt error contract reuses the strict nested steering error shape: 401 unauthenticated, 403 per existing auth resolution, 404 not_found for unknown run/node, 409 node_finished for terminal run/node or natural-empty close during the request, 422 not_steerable_here for detached/parked/absent/non-interrupt-capable handles, 500 internal_error. NO `not_interruptible` code.

Handler sequencing mirrors send: resolve auth (any authenticated member may steer; identity-less run allowed when install gate permits) → load run/events/pending interactions/projected state/registry handle → 404/409/422 checks with persisted lifecycle outranking a stale handle → re-read run status as final async DB gate → handle.interrupt() synchronously before any further await (no-torn-controller boundary) → await shared settlement and map outcome. Caller disconnect after the synchronous interrupt does not undo it.

Send route passes body.intent into one synchronous handle.accept(message, intent) — no await between the final gate and accept; the route never performs 'read sub-state then send_now' as two operations; returns result.receipt.state exactly (queued while generating/interrupting; awaiting_send_now while idle, including the message whose send_now releases the batch); duplicate message_id replays original receipt and cannot release idle twice.

WorkflowNodeState gains optional `steeringSubState?: 'generating' | 'idle-after-interrupt'` joined from the live in-process registry by exact (runId, nodeId) key AFTER terminal-settling persisted states — included only when the node is still running, the handle is live in this server process, interrupt-capable, and has a projected sub-state; omitted for queue-only non-Claude handles, parked asks, detached runs, terminal nodes, historical executions, absent handles; never persisted and never synthesized from transcript rows; `interrupting` is never projected.
openapi-defaults.ts unchanged (interrupt has no body; send keeps the steering validation hook for malformed JSON).

All 15 phase-3 route tests pass: live interrupt → 200 idle; natural-end race + pending guidance → 200 generating; natural-end race + empty → 409; repeated/concurrent interrupts share one abort and identical outcomes; interrupt while idle → idempotent 200 idle; actor ladder matches send; 404/409/422 ladder; terminal-after-initial-read → 409 no stale success; send Queue while idle → awaiting_send_now no wake; send_now while idle → awaiting_send_now + single wake old-then-new; duplicate send_now replays without second drain; send during interrupting → queued pending; GET-run projection only on the matching live interrupt-capable running node incl. namespaced loop-group body key; GET-run without qualifying handle wire-identical to today; generated OpenAPI contains route + response enum + optional field.

packages/web/src/lib/api.generated.d.ts regenerated via `bun --filter @archon/web generate:types` against a tracked dev server on port 3090 (reuse only a server known to belong to this worktree; otherwise start, record PID/port/worktree, stop only the one started); generated diff contains only the route/schemas above — unrelated churn is a failure; never hand-edited.

Interrupt request intentionally waits for classification — every engine close/park/discard/error path must settle it (proven in US-002); do NOT paper over a leaked promise with a route timeout. userStories.title: Both web docks, accessibility, and visual states
userStories.description: As an operator in either web shell, I want the dock to render Stop / Stopping / Send-now states with identical anatomy, copy, and behavior, so that I can interrupt a Claude turn and redirect it without losing text, focus, or context — while non-Claude nodes keep the queue-only dock.
acceptanceCriteria: packages/web/src/lib/steering-dock.ts extended with: projected agent sub-state, separate send vs interrupt in-flight state (single inFlight flag replaced — Queue stays usable while Stop is pending), local `interrupting` transient, intent-aware receipts keeping generated `queued | awaiting_send_now` union, reversible Send-now inFlightBatch, exact labels/copy/announcements, and route-neutral steering request error (rename SteeringSendError + normalizer; update both request layers and tests; wire unchanged).

Derived modes: queue-only handle (sub-state absent) → existing Story 2.1 Queue dock, no Stop; `generating` → Stop left + Queue right + `queued · n` band; local `interrupting` → focusable `Stopping…` aria-disabled (never native disabled, same DOM focus) + Queue still usable; `idle-after-interrupt` → no Stop + Send now + `will send · n` + exact disclosure; response `generating`/terminal → route outcome + authoritative run state. Absent sub-state means queue-only, NOT auto-detached (detached stays the 422/live-context decision).

Interrupt flow: Stop → local interrupting + one polite announcement `agent interrupting`; repeated Stop suppressed while focusable; 200 idle → render idle, announce `agent idle · Send now delivers`, focus LAST TRANSCRIPT ROW (scroller fallback, never send control, never <body> — Story 2.3 overrides the older EXPERIENCE.md note; record divergence in tests); 200 generating → announce `turn ended before stop · <n> sent · agent generating`, no fake interrupted row; 409 → clear transient, authoritative state removes dock, draft retained; 422 → existing refusal/disclosure path, draft/receipts kept; network/500 → back to generating, stable role-alert, retry allowed.

Queue during interrupting: Queue button + Cmd/Ctrl+Enter guarded only by non-blank draft + no send in flight + no pending ask — NOT blocked by interrupting; accepted receipt stays in band; if idle resolves, only heading/accessible label changes to Will send.

Send now: requires non-blank newly typed draft (existing queue alone never enables it); reducer snapshots displayed accepted receipts + pending new message into inFlightBatch and clears band optimistically; POSTs ONLY the new draft with stable retry UUID + intent 'send_now'; success → discard batch, clear only submitted text (preserve in-flight edits), derive generating, announce `agent generating`; failure → restore all snapshotted items at front in original order, preserve new message + retry id, stay idle unless terminal projection supersedes, render `couldn't send · back in the queue` in role="alert"; ambiguous retry reposts only the same new message id — never re-enqueues prior receipt ids.

Anatomy identical in both shells: (1) non-empty full-width receipt band, (2) idle-only disclosure `stopped after the last completed tool call · files already written stay written`, (3) labelled textarea, (4) role-alert failure/refusal or described blocked reason, (5) one control row — Stop/Stopping left, Queue/Send now right. Band headers lowercase in DOM (`queued · n`, `will send · n`) uppercased by CSS; list names `Queued messages, n` / `Will send, n`; visible send word starts accessible name + queue depth + keyboard hint; Queue/Send-now use aria-disabled (never disabled) off the shared submit predicate for click AND keyboard paths.

Styling: 32px minimum targets; Send now and Queue share stable ≥84px min width, never shift position; existing surface/border/text-secondary/accent-bright/focus tokens only; Stop and send bordered with transparent fill in BOTH shells (final DESIGN.md wins over the mock's filled-Legacy comment); `Stopping…` uses text-secondary ≥4.5:1; focus outlines ≥3:1 non-text per final measured shell tokens; no dock motion; existing transitions respect motion-reduce; band absent when empty, ≤33vh, scrolls independently; dock remains sibling of transcript scroller (never overlay/child).

Focus/announcements: exactly one polite role="status" region per mounted room/dock, set once per transition with the composite messages; delivery failure alone uses assertive role="alert"; only the actual last rendered history item is programmatically focusable (tabIndex=-1 or forwarded ref, not in Tab order); Stop unmount and dock removal focus that row with preventScroll (scroller fallback); reader scroll position preserved as dock grows/shrinks.

No third dock component; JSX stays shell-owned and thin; no cross-shell component import (console-isolation.test.ts green), no workflows-package import, no new breakpoint, no literal palette, no second state machine; `interrupting` never enters generated types or node lifecycle.

Component tests pass in both shells covering: semantic control/state table incl. no Stop for non-Claude queue-only node; Stopping… aria-disabled + focus retained + Queue keyboard/click still works + shared false predicate via aria-disabled; idle DOM order/copy/list labelling/empty-band; one polite update per transition + distinct delivery alert; Stop unmount/dock removal focus last row + scroller fallback + body never owns focus; run-payload idle renders without preceding local click; shared-logic tests cover mode derivation, each interrupt resolution, Queue-during-interrupting, Send-now non-blank gate, batch success/failure/retry-id stability, generated receipt states, exact strings.

userStories.title: Deterministic E2E evidence and closeout
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want deterministic Playwright evidence that a web-dispatched run can be interrupted and redirected on the same session in both shells for direct and loop paths, plus a complete acceptance map, so that Story 2.3 can be marked done with proof instead of timing luck.
acceptanceCriteria: e2e-fake provider gains strict opt-in `interruptible: true` scenario option validated to require emitTool:true + positive bounded delayMs: emits existing assistant chunk + tool call but not its result, waits on first of node abortSignal / turn interruptSignal / bounded delay, removes all listeners/timers; node abort → existing `Query aborted`; turn interrupt → matching tool_result with toolOutcome 'interrupted' then result with same session id + terminalReason 'aborted_tools'; natural delay → current success path; provided interruptSignal also has defined behavior outside the opt-in scenario (interrupted result; interrupted tool_result only when a tool was emitted); calls with no interrupt signal/event keep exact existing chunks.

e2e-fake unit tests cover: node-abort precedence, already-aborted signals, exactly-once listener cleanup, natural timeout, interrupt before/after tool emission, same-session result, unchanged default scenarios; `cd packages/providers && bun test src/e2e-fake/provider.test.ts && bun run type-check` pass.

Existing fixtures extended, NOT duplicated: e2e-queue-guidance.yaml first-turn directive adds `{"interruptible":true,"emitTool":true,"delayMs":30000}`; e2e-queue-guidance-loop.yaml adds `{"interruptible":true,"emitTool":true,"delayMs":25000}`; e2e/lib/playwright/archon-runtime.ts untouched; existing queue-guidance spec still green (Story 2.1 regression gate).

second

third` in same node occurrence/session → run finishes with no interrupted-turn node_failed/dag_node_failed.

Failure/race coverage: intercepted Send-now failure restores band old-then-new, new message retryable, exact role-alert copy, no old receipt re-POSTed; Queue during in-flight interrupt appears under Will send after idle; interrupt while idle → idempotent 200 idle; interrupt after terminal → 409 node_finished; natural-end generating/empty-finished races remain deterministic route/engine unit tests (no timing-flaky browser sleeps added).
